keyVerseText: For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.
rootMeaning: The root of דַּרְדַּע (Dardaʻ) is linked to דַּר (dar), which denotes a pearl or mother-of-pearl, emphasizing a luminous, precious quality. The etymology suggests 'pearl of knowledge,' combining the imagery of a radiant gem with wisdom. This literal sense enriches the common English gloss by highlighting not only the value but also the brilliance and rarity of the wisdom associated with the name.
usageInScripture: The word דַּרְדַּע appears only once in Scripture, specifically as a proper name in 1 Kings 4:31, where it is translated as 'and Darda.' This limited occurrence confirms its use as a personal name rather than a common noun, identifying an Israelite renowned for wisdom. The consistency in translation underscores the importance of Darda as a representative figure among the wise men of Israel, though ultimately surpassed by Solomon.
theologicalSignificance: Darda's name, meaning 'pearl of knowledge,' points to the precious and divine nature of true wisdom, which Scripture esteems highly. His inclusion among the four men of great fame for wisdom underscores God's gifting of understanding to His people. Yet, the text reminds us that even the greatest human wisdom pales in comparison to Solomon's God-given insight, foreshadowing the ultimate wisdom revealed in Christ. This teaches believers to value wisdom as a divine treasure but to seek the surpassing wisdom found in God alone.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Kings 4:31 highlights Solomon's unparalleled wisdom, stating he was wiser than Ethan, Heman, Chalcol, and Darda, all sons of Mahol famed for their insight. The mention of Darda here emphasizes the high standard of wisdom Solomon exceeded. Understanding Darda as the 'pearl of knowledge' deepens the verse's meaning by illustrating that Solomon's wisdom outshone even the most precious and radiant human understanding known at the time.
